vendoringPolicy: Pattern port only. The upstream hook and container were read to understand the interaction (persisted panel width published as a CSS custom property on the layout root, collapsed 8px rail that reopens on drag past an 8px threshold, double-click reset). No upstream file is copied or redistributed; Nexus reimplements the behaviour in its own TypeScript on top of the pre-existing mouse-driven mission splitter, its zustand store idiom (rail-width-store) and BEM CSS. Entries are therefore type 'adapted'.

files.changeSummary: Upstream persists a clamped width in localStorage from a pointer-driven hook and writes it to a CSS var on :root, with a separate collapsed-rail pointer handler that expands the owner after an 8px travel threshold and a double-click reset. Nexus keeps the persisted width in a zustand store (clamp band mirrors --nexus-shell-inspector-min/max; tolerant storage read/write), publishes it as --nexus-inspector-w on the mission board root via React style, reuses its existing window mousemove/mouseup/blur drag with a shared beginPointerDrag helper, and adds keyboard reopening (Enter/Space/Arrow) plus focus hand-off to the splitter. Stacked (height) mode stays session-only ratio state as before.

files.changeSummary: Upstream renders a framer-motion inspector sized by `width: var(--ao-inspector-w)` and, when collapsed, an absolutely positioned 8px-wide `inspector-collapsed-rail` with a resize cursor. Nexus renders the rail as a flex sibling of the graph with role=separator, aria-label/orientation/value*, tabIndex=0, a 2px focus-visible outline, a >=32px tall target, a 2x24px grip animated on opacity only (150ms --ease-out-quart, reduced-motion guarded) and a stacked-mode variant along the bottom edge. No framer-motion, no Tailwind, no upstream markup copied.
